input: This summary reviews delivery performance at a contract packaging firm that runs 2 plants with revenue of $63 million per year, and considers a recommendation to install a scheduling system at Plant 2 first, holding the other plants until Plant 2 results are reported; the operations director owns the scheduling programme. The evidence base is order records for 12 months, covering 15679 orders. On-time delivery over the last two quarters was 91%, against a target of 95%. Overtime cost was $2.6 million last year, up 19% on the year before, and the order backlog currently stands at 3.4 weeks, against 1.6 weeks a year ago. Plant 2 accounts for 61% of late orders. A scheduling system for all plants is quoted at $328k, while Plant 2 alone is $141k. An internal estimate, rather than a vendor figure, puts the overtime reduction at Plant 2 at 15-20% in the first year. Staging the installation in this way spends the smaller sum first and puts the wider rollout behind one plant's measured results, with extension to the remaining plant to follow if the reported figures improve as estimated.
